title: How chalk-talk proves every arrow
subtitle: from a scene file to a page you can trust

edges.label: writes the story
edges.inferred: your agent writes this file; there is no chalk-talk code to point at

steps.title: It starts as a story
steps.say: Your agent never draws. It writes a short **scene file**: what to show, what moves, what to say, and which lines of code back each arrow.

steps.title: One script builds it
steps.say: `build.mjs` reads the scene. Plain Node, no dependencies, the same on Windows, macOS and Linux.

steps.title: Real code comes along
steps.say: Every `code` field points at real lines. The builder copies them in, so a click on a block or an arrow shows the code.

steps.title: Every arrow gets checked
steps.say: For each arrow, the checker looks for its `calls` text inside the cited lines. Found: a **✓**. Missing: the build warns and the arrow turns red.

steps.title: Guesses stay guesses
steps.say: The first arrow has no line of code behind it, so it carries a **?** instead of pretending. Press `V` to see which hops are proven.

steps.title: Into the engine
steps.say: The checked scene drops into the engine's `__SCENE__` slot. Layout, routing and 3D drawing happen in the browser.

steps.title: A page you can send
steps.say: Out comes **one HTML file**. It works offline and opens the exact lines behind every part.

steps.title: The whole trip
steps.say: Story, build, read, check, page. Six hops traced to a line, one honest guess.
